title: Tenant attribute sync window causes authorization misbinding between sessions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: A timing window between tenant-attribute updates in the identity service and propagation to the edge/session cache can cause requests to be authorized with stale tenant attributes. In practice this produced intermittent cross-tenant authorization where a valid session token was accepted but associated tenant-scopes were incorrect for ~1-3s after an org attribute change (role change, tenant move, or API key rebind) leading to privilege exposure for some hosted and Dedicated customers. Private deployments with local introspection can manifest similar behavior when the local attribute sync cron falls behind (on heavy load or during HA failover).

Observed behavior:
- Token introspection returns is_active = true, but tenant_id attribute is stale for a short window.
- Edge layer reads cached session->tenant mapping and allows request to proceed against resources of the old tenant before the new mapping is propagated.
- Customers reported reads/writes appearing under the wrong org in audit logs and three escalations opened by a high-security customer ("Acme Health") and one Dedicated customer.

Environments impacted: hosted API (primary), Dedicated clusters with shared attribute cache, Private deployments running older sync agents.

First detection: 2026-03-11 22:30 UTC via alert 'auth.audit.tenant-mismatch-rate' and direct customer report. Initial triage showed correlation with tenant attribute writes and high traffic on the edge routing cache.

Reproduction steps (dev):
1) Create two tenants T1 and T2 and an API key bound to T1.
2) Use API key to establish session and perform a write to a T1-scoped resource.
3) Update tenant binding for the API key to T2 via org migration API.
4) Within 1-3s, send a new request using same token and observe resource access scope: some requests succeed against T1 resources (stale) instead of being rejected or routed to T2.

Root cause hypothesis: the edge/session layer caches a compact tenant-mapping (session_id -> tenant_id) keyed by session token. The identity service updates tenant attributes in the primary store and emits an async change event. A race exists where the edge cache is not invalidated on the same event stream partition, so in the window between write and event consumption the edge serves requests with old mapping. Dedicated clusters with multi-region replication exhibited longer windows due to queue backlog. Private customers with disabled immediate invalidation experienced similar but longer windows.

Impact scope: 2 high-severity escalations (Acme Health, FinNova), approximately 12 smaller orgs showed transient mismatches in logs. No confirmed data exfiltration detected, but audit integrity was violated and customer trust impacted.

Mitigation applied (short-term):
- Deployed a hotfix to the edge that checks token issued_at vs tenant-update-timestamp on introspection for high-risk routes (canary hosted region eu-west-1) to reject tokens if tenant_update_ts > token_last_checked_ts.
- For Dedicated customers, enabled immediate in-memory invalidation via admin path where available.
- Notified affected customers and opened support tickets with recommended mitigation steps for private deployments (restart sync agent or enable pull-on-write config).

Long-term fix: ensure strong cache invalidation contract between identity service and edge/session cache: add synchronous invalidation API during tenant-attribute mutating operations and fallback to event-stream invalidation. Rework session cache to store attribute version and validate on each request with a bounded cheap read from a version store to avoid full introspection on every request.

Links: Confluence runbook: https://confluence.internal.redwood/auth/ENG-46100 , Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234567/p1678584000000000 , PR-for-hotfix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/7832 (canary), Support ticket: SUP-9981
comments: 2026-03-12 09:20 UTC - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after customer report. Initial triage indicates cache invalidation gap. Marking P0 due to customer escalations.
2026-03-12 12:45 UTC - Marco Li: Reproduced locally following steps in description. Confirm race between event consumer and edge cache invalidation on heavy load. Attached replication script to PR.

2026-03-13 03:10 UTC - PagerDuty run on-call (Nora Singh): Deployed temporary gate in eu-west-1 that performs a lightweight version check against identity service for tokens updated in last 10s. Observed drop in mismatch alerts by ~90% in canary.
2026-03-13 22:00 UTC - Customer Success (Jorge Ramos): Notified Acme Health and FinNova; both accepted temporary mitigation. Two Dedicated clusters agreed to in-place cache invalidation enablement.
2026-03-14 07:30 UTC - Marco Li: Opened RFC for synchronous invalidation endpoint and design doc attached to Confluence. Planning full rollout with feature flag in runtime-1.22.

acceptance_criteria: Edge rejects or revalidates requests if tenant attribute version on identity store is newer than cached mapping within configured window
No tenant-mismatch audit alerts for the canary region for 24h post-rollout under simulated churn test
Automated regression test that simulates attribute change + concurrent requests included in CI with under-50ms median invalidation latency
Dedicated clusters can opt into immediate invalidation and show no mismatch during a 2-hour soak under production-like traffic
Private deployment guidance written and validated with two pilot customers
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary - eu-west-1): deploy hotfix gate that validates attribute version (already in canary) - 2026-03-13 to 2026-03-15
Stage 2 (hosted): progressive rollout to remaining regions with metrics gating (tenant_mismatch_rate, error_rate) - 48h window per region
Stage 3 (Dedicated): coordinate with Dedicated account owners, enable in-place invalidation and monitor for 24h
Stage 4 (Private): communicate recommended config change and provide tooling to restart sync agent or enable pull-on-write; schedule follow-ups with impacted customers
Stage 5: deploy synchronous invalidation API and flag off by default; turn on incremental customers after validation
postmortem_actions: Implement synchronous invalidation API and deprecate long-lived unvalidated cache windows
Add end-to-end test in CI simulating tenant attribute write -> request flood to prevent regression
Instrument detailed per-tenant metrics and make tenant_mismatch_rate an automated incident signal
Update runbooks and customer-facing docs describing expected propagation windows and admin controls
Engage security to review potential blast radius and produce a compliance statement for affected customers
